extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys, and applicants (Finland / WIPO SCP readers)
extracted.subtask_short: inventive step and sufficiency for patents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to assess inventive step (obviousness) and sufficiency of disclosure under Finnish law, including definitions (person skilled in the art), methodologies (problem–solution), statutory requirements for the description/claims, and special rules for biological material. Intended to guide patent examination, opposition, limitation, and validity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person skilled in the art (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The average person skilled in the art is an ordinary skilled practitioner who is aware of prior art at the date of filing (priority date), has knowledge of the state of the art, and has at their disposal the ordinary means and capacity to carry out routine work and experimentation, as well as the capacity to use prior art as is usual for the technical field. May be considered a group in some high‑tech or complex fields. Not a highly skilled expert; the patent examiner is not the person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the model to assess inventive step; examiners must avoid using their own subjective viewpoint. The skilled person can combine cited documents with common general knowledge (e.g., handbook teachings). In some cases (e.g., computing, ICs, complex chemical combinations) consider a group (research/working group) rather than a single person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (not obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention involves an inventive step if, having regard to the state of the art, it is not obvious to a person skilled in the art. Assessment asks whether it would have been obvious at the filing date, compared with the state of the art, to arrive at a result within the scope of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Obvious' means something that does not go beyond the normal progress of technology but follows plainly or logically from the prior art — i.e., something which does not involve the exercise of any skill or ability beyond that to be expected of the person skilled in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem–solution approach (methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Finnish Office predominantly applies the problem–solution approach of the European Patent Office to assess whether an invention involves an inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PRH Search and Examination Guidelines sections E.3.5.2 (Problem–solution approach) and related sections (E.3.5). Use this structured methodology when evaluating inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects supporting inventiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors or aspects that may support a finding of inventiveness are identified in PRH guidance (section E.3.5.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to PRH guidelines for examples and explanations of aspects that can support inventiveness (e.g., unexpected technical effect, long‑felt but unmet need, superior properties). The page references this section but does not reproduce the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enabling disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall be sufficiently clear to enable a person skilled in the art, with the guidance thereof, to carry out the invention (Patents Act, Section 8, subsection 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiency is judged by whether the skilled person can practice the invention based on the disclosure. For biological material, see specific deposit rules (Section 8a). Non‑enablement can be a ground for revocation/invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological material deposit requirement (Section 8a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an invention concerns biological material not publicly available or not describable in the application so as to enable the skilled person, a sample must be deposited no later than the filing date and kept continuously on deposit so any entitled person may obtain a sample in Finland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposits must meet governmental rules on where to deposit. Failure to comply means the invention is not regarded as disclosed with sufficient clarity in the cases referred to in Section 8a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: general part requirements (Patent Regulations, Section 4(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must comprise a general part illustrating the scope of application of the invention and the technique upon which it is based, i.e., the state of the art. Presentation of the state of the art must include references to literature known to the applicant, and must present the special features of the invention over the state of the art, as well as the means necessary for achieving them. This presentation must conform to the presentation given in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the invention cannot be industrially exploited, this must be stated. The general part should make clear how the invention differs from and improves upon the cited prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description: specific part requirements (Patent Regulations, Section 4(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must include a specific part describing the invention in detail, primarily by giving examples or embodiments and possibly referring to a drawing. The invention must be illustrated with examples so that the claims can be considered substantiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings are included, provide a list of figures as an introduction to the specific part. Examples/embodiments should enable the skilled person to carry out the invention and substantiate the claimed scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation when multiple independent and dependent claims are present (Patent Regulations, Section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claims contain several independent claims, the inventions corresponding to them are to be presented in the description as specified in Section 4. Subject matter of dependent claims must be presented in the description to such extent as is necessary for the claim to be understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include embodiments corresponding to dependent claims (the specific part is normally sufficient). Ensure each independent claim is supported by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must disclose special characteristics necessary for intended effect (Patent Regulations, Section 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim must disclose those special characteristics that are necessary for achieving the intended effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should contain the essential technical features that produce the alleged technical effect; lack of these may render claims unsupported or unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity/searchability of claims (PRH guideline C.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be clear and searchable (Patents Office guidance on clarity/searchable claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See PRH Search and Examination Guidelines C.1.3 for specifics on drafting clear, examinable claims and avoiding ambiguity that hampers search and examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (PRH guideline E.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention disclosure must enable reproducibility (toistettavuus) such that a person skilled in the art can reproduce the invention (PRH guideline E.1.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether examples and description provide sufficient information for routine practice and experimentation; irreproducible disclosures may fail the sufficiency requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revocation/invalidity (Sections 25 and 52)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be revoked or declared invalid if: (1) the patent relates to an invention that does not satisfy the statutory requirements (Sections 1, 1a, 1b or 2); (2) the description is not sufficiently clear to enable a person skilled in the art to carry out the invention; (3) the patent contains subject matter not included in the application as filed; or (4) the scope of protection was extended after the relevant notice (Sections 25(1) and 52(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory grounds are the key legal criteria applied in oppositions and invalidity actions; ensure examination and claim amendments avoid added matter and extension of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for acceptance of a request to limit a patent (Section 53b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request to limit a patent will be accepted only if: (1) the patent refers to an invention presented with sufficient clarity for a person skilled in the art to use the invention; (2) the patent does not involve anything that does not appear from the application as filed; and (3) the scope of protection has not been extended from that of the patent granted or from the previously decided scope of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing for limitation, ensure the amended patent meets clarity, no‑added‑matter, and no‑extension requirements; these mirror revocation/invalidity standards.
